FPIA: vendor pure-Python PyYAML 6.0.1 so the FPIA tests run where PyYAML is not installed

Fix round 2 (G1) made track_c_fpia_workflows.py read workflow files with PyYAML. The owner full-suite
workflows install only pytest and numpy, so on PR CI every FPIA test that reaches the workflow analysis
went NOT_RUN or failed with ModuleNotFoundError (60 failed in the offline jobs).

- tools/integration/_vendor/yaml: lib/yaml/*.py of the upstream PyYAML-6.0.1 sdist (sha256 bfdf460b...),
  byte for byte, with its MIT LICENSE; cyaml.py left out (it imports the compiled yaml._yaml by absolute
  name). README.md records the provenance and every file digest. No bytecode committed.
- track_c_fpia_workflows.py imports the vendored copy (package or script mode), never an installed one;
  loader_info() also records the source and with_libyaml. Detection logic unchanged.
- track-c-fpia.yml no longer installs PyYAML; the G7 test now asserts that.
- test_integration_fpia_vendor.py pins the vendored files to the README digests, checks no bytecode or
  extension modules are tracked, and that both import modes load _vendor/yaml without libyaml.
- test_integration_fpia_self.py: FPIA's self-placement check now includes the vendored files.

Packaging only: no FPIA check, status or threshold changed. Frozen tools, Track C files and owner paths
untouched.

FPIA: vendor pure-Python PyYAML 6.0.1 so the FPIA tests run where PyYAML is not installed

Fix round 2 (G1) made track_c_fpia_workflows.py read workflow files with PyYAML. The owner full-suite
workflows install only pytest and numpy, so on PR CI every FPIA test that reaches the workflow analysis
went NOT_RUN or failed with ModuleNotFoundError (60 failed in the offline jobs).

- tools/integration/_vendor/yaml: lib/yaml/*.py of the upstream PyYAML-6.0.1 sdist (sha256 bfdf460b...),
  byte for byte, with its MIT LICENSE; cyaml.py left out (it imports the compiled yaml._yaml by absolute
  name). README.md records the provenance and every file digest. No bytecode committed.
- track_c_fpia_workflows.py imports the vendored copy (package or script mode), never an installed one;
  loader_info() also records the source and with_libyaml. Detection logic unchanged.
- track-c-fpia.yml no longer installs PyYAML; the G7 test now asserts that.
- test_integration_fpia_vendor.py pins the vendored files to the README digests, checks no bytecode or
  extension modules are tracked, and that both import modes load _vendor/yaml without libyaml.
- test_integration_fpia_self.py: FPIA's self-placement check now includes the vendored files.

Packaging only: no FPIA check, status or threshold changed. Frozen tools, Track C files and owner paths
untouched.

FPIA: vendor pure-Python PyYAML 6.0.1 so the FPIA tests run where PyYAML is not installed

Fix round 2 (G1) made track_c_fpia_workflows.py read workflow files with PyYAML. The owner full-suite
workflows install only pytest and numpy, so on PR CI every FPIA test that reaches the workflow analysis
went NOT_RUN or failed with ModuleNotFoundError (60 failed in the offline jobs).

- tools/integration/_vendor/yaml: lib/yaml/*.py of the upstream PyYAML-6.0.1 sdist (sha256 bfdf460b...),
  byte for byte, with its MIT LICENSE; cyaml.py left out (it imports the compiled yaml._yaml by absolute
  name). README.md records the provenance and every file digest. No bytecode committed.
- track_c_fpia_workflows.py imports the vendored copy (package or script mode), never an installed one;
  loader_info() also records the source and with_libyaml. Detection logic unchanged.
- track-c-fpia.yml no longer installs PyYAML; the G7 test now asserts that.
- test_integration_fpia_vendor.py pins the vendored files to the README digests, checks no bytecode or
  extension modules are tracked, and that both import modes load _vendor/yaml without libyaml.
- test_integration_fpia_self.py: FPIA's self-placement check now includes the vendored files.

Packaging only: no FPIA check, status or threshold changed. Frozen tools, Track C files and owner paths
untouched.

Fix round 2 (G1) made track_c_fpia_workflows.py read workflow files with PyYAML. The owner full-suite
workflows install only pytest and numpy, so on PR CI every FPIA test that reaches the workflow analysis
went NOT_RUN or failed with ModuleNotFoundError (60 failed in the offline jobs).

  byte for byte, with its MIT LICENSE; cyaml.py left out (it imports the compiled yaml._yaml by absolute
  name). README.md records the provenance and every file digest. No bytecode committed.

  loader_info() also records the source and with_libyaml. Detection logic unchanged.
- track-c-fpia.yml no longer installs PyYAML; the G7 test now asserts that.
- test_integration_fpia_vendor.py pins the vendored files to the README digests, checks no bytecode or
  extension modules are tracked, and that both import modes load _vendor/yaml without libyaml.
- test_integration_fpia_self.py: FPIA's self-placement check now includes the vendored files.

Packaging only: no FPIA check, status or threshold changed. Frozen tools, Track C files and owner paths
untouched.

FPIA: vendor pure-Python PyYAML 6.0.1 so the FPIA tests run where PyYAML is not installed

Fix round 2 (G1) made track_c_fpia_workflows.py read workflow files with PyYAML. The owner full-suite
workflows install only pytest and numpy, so on PR CI every FPIA test that reaches the workflow analysis
went NOT_RUN or failed with ModuleNotFoundError (60 failed in the offline jobs).

- tools/integration/_vendor/yaml: lib/yaml/*.py of the upstream PyYAML-6.0.1 sdist (sha256 bfdf460b...),
  byte for byte, with its MIT LICENSE; cyaml.py left out (it imports the compiled yaml._yaml by absolute
  name). README.md records the provenance and every file digest. No bytecode committed.
- track_c_fpia_workflows.py imports the vendored copy (package or script mode), never an installed one;
  loader_info() also records the source and with_libyaml. Detection logic unchanged.
- track-c-fpia.yml no longer installs PyYAML; the G7 test now asserts that.
- test_integration_fpia_vendor.py pins the vendored files to the README digests, checks no bytecode or
  extension modules are tracked, and that both import modes load _vendor/yaml without libyaml.
- test_integration_fpia_self.py: FPIA's self-placement check now includes the vendored files.

Packaging only: no FPIA check, status or threshold changed. Frozen tools, Track C files and owner paths
untouched.

c","tree_id":"18de1b11a0ed6cd64150937c362baa822a8e4943","message":"[proposal] FPIA: vendor pure-Python PyYAML 6.0.1 so the FPIA tests run where PyYAML is not installed

Fix round 2 (G1) made track_c_fpia_workflows.py read workflow files with PyYAML. The owner full-suite
workflows install only pytest and numpy, so on PR CI every FPIA test that reaches the workflow analysis
went NOT_RUN or failed with ModuleNotFoundError (60 failed in the offline jobs).

- tools/integration/_vendor/yaml: lib/yaml/*.py of the upstream PyYAML-6.0.1 sdist (sha256 bfdf460b...),
  byte for byte, with its MIT LICENSE; cyaml.py left out (it imports the compiled yaml._yaml by absolute
  name). README.md records the provenance and every file digest. No bytecode committed.
- track_c_fpia_workflows.py imports the vendored copy (package or script mode), never an installed one;
  loader_info() also records the source and with_libyaml. Detection logic unchanged.
- track-c-fpia.yml no longer installs PyYAML; the G7 test now asserts that.
- test_integration_fpia_vendor.py pins the vendored files to the README digests, checks no bytecode or
  extension modules are tracked, and that both import modes load _vendor/yaml without libyaml.
- test_integration_fpia_self.py: FPIA's self-placement check now includes the vendored files.

Packaging only: no FPIA check, status or threshold changed. Frozen tools, Track C files and owner paths
untouched.

FPIA: vendor pure-Python PyYAML 6.0.1 so the FPIA tests run where PyYAML is not installed

Fix round 2 (G1) made track_c_fpia_workflows.py read workflow files with PyYAML. The owner full-suite
workflows install only pytest and numpy, so on PR CI every FPIA test that reaches the workflow analysis
went NOT_RUN or failed with ModuleNotFoundError (60 failed in the offline jobs).

- tools/integration/_vendor/yaml: lib/yaml/*.py of the upstream PyYAML-6.0.1 sdist (sha256 bfdf460b...),
  byte for byte, with its MIT LICENSE; cyaml.py left out (it imports the compiled yaml._yaml by absolute
  name). README.md records the provenance and every file digest. No bytecode committed.
- track_c_fpia_workflows.py imports the vendored copy (package or script mode), never an installed one;
  loader_info() also records the source and with_libyaml. Detection logic unchanged.
- track-c-fpia.yml no longer installs PyYAML; the G7 test now asserts that.
- test_integration_fpia_vendor.py pins the vendored files to the README digests, checks no bytecode or
  extension modules are tracked, and that both import modes load _vendor/yaml without libyaml.
- test_integration_fpia_self.py: FPIA's self-placement check now includes the vendored files.

Packaging only: no FPIA check, status or threshold changed. Frozen tools, Track C files and owner paths
untouched.

Fix round 2 (G1) made track_c_fpia_workflows.py read workflow files with PyYAML. The owner full-suite
workflows install only pytest and numpy, so on PR CI every FPIA test that reaches the workflow analysis
went NOT_RUN or failed with ModuleNotFoundError (60 failed in the offline jobs).

  byte for byte, with its MIT LICENSE; cyaml.py left out (it imports the compiled yaml._yaml by absolute
  name). README.md records the provenance and every file digest. No bytecode committed.

  loader_info() also records the source and with_libyaml. Detection logic unchanged.

- test_integration_fpia_vendor.py pins the vendored files to the README digests, checks no bytecode or
  extension modules are tracked, and that both import modes load _vendor/yaml without libyaml.
- test_integration_fpia_self.py: FPIA's self-placement check now includes the vendored files.

Packaging only: no FPIA check, status or threshold changed. Frozen tools, Track C files and owner paths
untouched.

FPIA: vendor pure-Python PyYAML 6.0.1 so the FPIA tests run where PyYAML is not installed

Fix round 2 (G1) made track_c_fpia_workflows.py read workflow files with PyYAML. The owner full-suite
workflows install only pytest and numpy, so on PR CI every FPIA test that reaches the workflow analysis
went NOT_RUN or failed with ModuleNotFoundError (60 failed in the offline jobs).

- tools/integration/_vendor/yaml: lib/yaml/*.py of the upstream PyYAML-6.0.1 sdist (sha256 bfdf460b...),
  byte for byte, with its MIT LICENSE; cyaml.py left out (it imports the compiled yaml._yaml by absolute
  name). README.md records the provenance and every file digest. No bytecode committed.
- track_c_fpia_workflows.py imports the vendored copy (package or script mode), never an installed one;
  loader_info() also records the source and with_libyaml. Detection logic unchanged.
- track-c-fpia.yml no longer installs PyYAML; the G7 test now asserts that.
- test_integration_fpia_vendor.py pins the vendored files to the README digests, checks no bytecode or
  extension modules are tracked, and that both import modes load _vendor/yaml without libyaml.
- test_integration_fpia_self.py: FPIA's self-placement check now includes the vendored files.

Packaging only: no FPIA check, status or threshold changed. Frozen tools, Track C files and owner paths
untouched.

FPIA: vendor pure-Python PyYAML 6.0.1 so the FPIA tests run where PyYAML is not installed

Fix round 2 (G1) made track_c_fpia_workflows.py read workflow files with PyYAML. The owner full-suite
workflows install only pytest and numpy, so on PR CI every FPIA test that reaches the workflow analysis
went NOT_RUN or failed with ModuleNotFoundError (60 failed in the offline jobs).

- tools/integration/_vendor/yaml: lib/yaml/*.py of the upstream PyYAML-6.0.1 sdist (sha256 bfdf460b...),
  byte for byte, with its MIT LICENSE; cyaml.py left out (it imports the compiled yaml._yaml by absolute
  name). README.md records the provenance and every file digest. No bytecode committed.
- track_c_fpia_workflows.py imports the vendored copy (package or script mode), never an installed one;
  loader_info() also records the source and with_libyaml. Detection logic unchanged.
- track-c-fpia.yml no longer installs PyYAML; the G7 test now asserts that.
- test_integration_fpia_vendor.py pins the vendored files to the README digests, checks no bytecode or
  extension modules are tracked, and that both import modes load _vendor/yaml without libyaml.
- test_integration_fpia_self.py: FPIA's self-placement check now includes the vendored files.

Packaging only: no FPIA check, status or threshold changed. Frozen tools, Track C files and owner paths
untouched.

FPIA: vendor pure-Python PyYAML 6.0.1 so the FPIA tests run where PyYAML is not installed

Fix round 2 (G1) made track_c_fpia_workflows.py read workflow files with PyYAML. The owner full-suite
workflows install only pytest and numpy, so on PR CI every FPIA test that reaches the workflow analysis
went NOT_RUN or failed with ModuleNotFoundError (60 failed in the offline jobs).

- tools/integration/_vendor/yaml: lib/yaml/*.py of the upstream PyYAML-6.0.1 sdist (sha256 bfdf460b...),
  byte for byte, with its MIT LICENSE; cyaml.py left out (it imports the compiled yaml._yaml by absolute
  name). README.md records the provenance and every file digest. No bytecode committed.
- track_c_fpia_workflows.py imports the vendored copy (package or script mode), never an installed one;
  loader_info() also records the source and with_libyaml. Detection logic unchanged.
- track-c-fpia.yml no longer installs PyYAML; the G7 test now asserts that.
- test_integration_fpia_vendor.py pins the vendored files to the README digests, checks no bytecode or
  extension modules are tracked, and that both import modes load _vendor/yaml without libyaml.
- test_integration_fpia_self.py: FPIA's self-placement check now includes the vendored files.

Packaging only: no FPIA check, status or threshold changed. Frozen tools, Track C files and owner paths
untouched.
